---
title: Release scheduling
code-annotations: hover
---

Course material can be released automatically by combining a publication
schedule with a recurring GitHub Actions build. The
`scheduled-docs-profiles` extension decides which documents are drafts at
render time; GitHub Actions renders the project regularly and deploys the
result to GitHub Pages.

This page uses an `exercise` profile for learner-facing material and a
`solution` profile for answer-bearing material. For more background, see
[Quarto profiles](profiles.qmd), [Quarto extensions](quarto-extensions.qmd),
and [GitHub Pages & Actions](github-pages.qmd).

## Publication flow

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    A["Hourly GitHub Actions run"] --> B["Render exercise profile"]
    B --> C["Evaluate exercise schedule"]
    C --> D["Render solution profile"]
    D --> E["Evaluate solution schedule"]
    E --> F["Deploy combined site to GitHub Pages"]
```

Scheduling a document does not cause GitHub Pages to update by itself. The
recurring workflow is what rebuilds the site after a release time has passed.

## Install the extensions

From the Quarto project directory, install the scheduling extension and the
solution filters used by the project:

```bash
quarto install extension au-mbg/quarto-teaching-tools/extensions/scheduled-docs-profiles
quarto install extension au-mbg/quarto-teaching-tools/extensions/callout-solution
quarto install extension au-mbg/quarto-teaching-tools/extensions/strip-solution
```

The commands install files below `_extensions/`. Commit that directory so
local and GitHub Actions builds use the same extension versions. A project
only needs both solution filters when it uses both authoring patterns shown
below.

## Configure the Quarto project

The base `_quarto.yml` enables the filters, hides draft pages from the
published website, and loads the metadata generated by the scheduling
extension:

```yaml
project:
  type: website

profile:
  group:
    - [exercise, solution]

website:
  title: "Course website"
  draft-mode: gone

metadata-files:
  - scheduled-docs_files/draft-list.yml

filters:
  - callout-solution
  - strip-solution
```

Set the output directory and solution visibility explicitly in each profile.
The exercise site is written to the root of `_site`; solutions are added
below `_site/solution`.

```yaml
# _quarto-exercise.yml
project:
  output-dir: _site

teaching:
  show-solutions: false
```

```yaml
# _quarto-solution.yml
project:
  output-dir: _site/solution

teaching:
  show-solutions: true
  default-solution-title: "Solution"
```

The profile group makes `exercise` and `solution` mutually exclusive. Always
pass the intended profile in publication commands rather than relying on a
developer's most recently used profile.

## Create release calendars

Use `_schedule.yml` as the exercise calendar. The extension looks for
`_schedule-<profile>.yml` first and falls back to `_schedule.yml` when a
profile-specific file does not exist. The exercise profile therefore uses the
base calendar in this example:

```yaml
# _schedule.yml
scheduled-docs:
  draft-after: "system-time"
  timezone: "+01:00"
  docs:
    - href: exercises/week-01.qmd
      date: "2026-09-07"
    - href: exercises/week-02.qmd
      date: "2026-09-14"
    - href: exercises/review.qmd
      date: "2099-01-01"
      draft: false
```

Create `_schedule-solution.yml` when solutions should follow a different
calendar:

```yaml
# _schedule-solution.yml
scheduled-docs:
  draft-after: "system-time"
  timezone: "+01:00"
  docs:
    - href: exercises/week-01.qmd
      date: "2026-09-08"
    - href: exercises/week-02.qmd
      date: "2026-09-15"
    - href: exercises/review.qmd
      date: "2026-09-20"
      draft: true
```

Each `href` is relative to the Quarto project directory. Dates use ISO
`YYYY-MM-DD` format and take effect at midnight in the configured fixed-offset
timezone. Use the offset that should apply on the release date; fixed offsets
do not adjust automatically for daylight-saving time.

Normally, keep `draft-after: "system-time"`. A future document is treated as
a draft. An explicit `draft: false` publishes a document regardless of its
future date, while `draft: true` withholds it regardless of a past date.

Separate calendars allow an exercise to appear before its worked solution.
If `_schedule-solution.yml` is absent, the solution profile falls back to
`_schedule.yml` and both versions follow the same dates.

## Combine scheduling with exercises and solutions

Scheduling controls whether the complete page is published. The solution
filters control which parts of a published page appear in each profile.

Use a solution callout for an instructor or solution-only explanation:

```markdown
::: {.callout-solution title="Worked solution"}
The completed calculation goes here.
:::
```

Use paired blocks when the two versions need different content:

<pre><code>::: &#123;teaching="exercise"&#125;
Complete the calculation.
:::

::: &#123;teaching="solution"&#125;
The completed calculation and explanation.
:::
</code></pre>

The same markers work on executable code cells:

<pre><code>```&#123;python&#125;
#| teaching: exercise
#| eval: false
# Complete this function.
```

```&#123;python&#125;
#| teaching: solution
def answer():
    return 42
```
</code></pre>

The `exercise` profile keeps exercise blocks and removes solution blocks; the
`solution` profile does the reverse. Setting `teaching.show-solutions`
explicitly is important because filtering content based only on a profile
name is less clear and less portable.

## Add local render tasks

Define a Pixi task that renders both outputs in the same order used by the
publication workflow:

```toml
[tasks.render]
args = [{ "arg" = "profile", default = "exercise",
          choices = ["exercise", "solution"] }]
cmd = "quarto render --profile {{profile}}"

[tasks.render-all]
cmd = "quarto render --profile exercise && quarto render --profile solution"
depends-on = ["clean"]

[tasks.clean]
cmd = "rm -rf _site .quarto"
```

Run `pixi run render-all` before publishing to inspect the same combined
output that GitHub Pages will receive. Serve `_site` with a local web server
when checking links between the root site and `/solution/`.

For authoring, use `quarto preview --profile exercise` or `quarto preview
--profile solution`. Quarto preview makes drafts visible and can reuse
previously generated HTML, so it does **not** reproduce the public release
state. Use a clean production render to verify whether scheduled pages will
actually be deployed.

## Rebuild and deploy on a schedule

Create `.github/workflows/publish.yml` with push, manual, and scheduled
triggers:

```yaml
name: Build and publish website

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
  schedule:
    - cron: "17 3 * * *" # <1>

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: prefix-dev/setup-pixi@v0.9.4
        with:
          pixi-version: v0.80.0
          cache: true

      - run: pixi run render-all

      - name: Upload Pages artifact
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: _site

  deploy:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4
```
1. This line defines the cron schedule. 

GitHub interprets the cron expression in UTC. This example requests one run per day at 03.17. Scheduled workflows can be delayed during periods of high load, so an eligible page normally appears during the next successful build rather than at an exact minute. Choose a cadence appropriate for the course; more frequent builds consume more Actions minutes.

Under the repository's **Settings → Pages**, set the deployment source to
**GitHub Actions**. Run the workflow manually once and inspect its build andd eployment jobs before relying on the schedule.

::: {.callout-warning}
Publishing solutions below `/solution/` separates the two versions for
navigation and scheduling, but it does not restrict access. Anyone who knows
or discovers the URL can open the solution site. Do not publish confidential
or access-controlled answer material this way.
:::

## Check a scheduled release

Before the course begins:

1. Confirm that every scheduled `href` matches a source document.
2. Run `pixi run render-all` and inspect both `_site` and `_site/solution`.
3. Check that exercise and solution dates use the intended timezone and
   ordering.
4. Trigger the GitHub Actions workflow manually and inspect the deployed site.
5. After a scheduled date passes, confirm that the next workflow run succeeds
   and that the expected page appears.

When a release does not appear, first inspect the Actions run, then reproduce
`pixi run render-all` locally. Common causes are a missing schedule entry, an
incorrect `href`, invalid YAML, a render failure, or a GitHub Pages artifact
path that does not match the configured output directory.
